analysis:
Reviewed StandaloneServer.swift lazy-load path in BASE 1780-2291 and HEAD 1-587. The HEAD change region (1964-1969, 1999-2006) is visible only through a truncated patch excerpt.

BASE behavior: for GLM plans, it computed a SHA-256 over the weights before load (1964-1965) and required that it equal manifest.aggregateSHA256 (1966-1969). It then called weights.recheck() (1970). It recomputed the hash after load and required the same match (2001-2004). The bracketed hash fed modelArtifactSHA256 and cacheEligibleWeightHash via reusableSSDWeightHashDecision (2008-2026). That value binds SSD prefix-cache entries and artifact identity (T-041 weightHash binding; A-004/T-012/T-027 weight substitution).

HEAD behavior: for GLM, the pre-load hash is skipped (required: artifactIdentityRequired && glmPlan == nil). preLoadArtifactHash is now a var, and only recheck() runs before load. The new comment says the managed GLM load SHA-256-verifies every manifest file before serving and that its verified digest replaces both bracketing passes. The post-load replacement code is truncated, so I cannot see how postLoadArtifactHash and preLoadArtifactHash are populated for GLM.

Integration must verify:
1. GLM5NextManagedLoad / loadServingContainer really hashes the same bytes it maps or loads, so there is no TOCTOU between verification and use.
2. It fails closed on a manifest mismatch.
3. The digest assigned into the bracket decision is that verified digest, not an unverified manifest constant.
4. The .changed and .unavailable paths still work, so an operator swapping weights mid-load cannot yield a cacheEligibleWeightHash or modelArtifactSHA256 that misattributes identity.

Non-GLM paths are unchanged. No regression is provable from the visible evidence, so I report no finding. Deeper review is requested for the truncated head region and the GLM5NextManagedLoad verification implementation.
